measuredOn: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 16 threads, Fedora 44, Node v24.14.1, npm run build. Unlike tests/long-journal/budgets.json's timing budgets this carries no machine-speed multiplier - the same source and the same lockfile gzip to close to the same byte count on any machine - but it is not bit-for-bit reproducible either: five straight rebuilds of one commit, no source change between them, gzipped to 295868-295884B. Vite/Rollup's content hashing is not fully deterministic run to run. gzipBytesBudget carries a 1024B floor over the baseline for exactly that (GZIP_WOBBLE_FLOOR_BYTES in check-first-load-budget.mjs), the same job FLOOR_MS does for the timing budgets. filesBudget carries none - the file count was the same 111 across all five rebuilds. Seeded at 295873B across 111 files for phase 9 audit ticket 01, which is the ratchet tickets 02 and 03 tighten rather than a target anybody has agreed. Re-record with `node scripts/check-first-load-budget.mjs --record` after a change that is meant to grow the first-load graph, and paste the printed block in here. Ticket 03 tightened it on 2026-09-06, on this same machine: 258412B across 109 files, from deferring the archive and hormone-curve areas out of journal.ts's composition and moving fractionalEpochDay off the path that kept the curve models in the graph anyway. Its baseline is not the 295873B above but a fresh measurement of main taken the same afternoon, 295878B across the same 111 files, because tickets 02, 04 and the migration squash had all landed in between and none of them re-recorded here. So the cut is 37466B, 12.7%, and two fewer round trips. Worth knowing before anyone reads that pair of numbers as the whole story: ticket 02 did remove the 22.5KB d3-shape/d3-scale chunk from the first load and main carries no d3 chunk any more, yet main's total is within 5B of what ticket 01 recorded before it - something else that landed in the same window replaced d3's bytes one for one, and nobody has looked at what.

firstLoad.what: every /_app/immutable URL build/index.html asks for, gzipped

onDemand.what: the OCR engine and the standard PDF fonts - not first-load, but the largest thing the app can ask for. Recorded rather than gated: nothing on a first visit waits on it.
